लोह १

LOHA I . An asura. When the pāṇḍavas were living incognito they kept their weapons in a secret place. Availing of this opportunity loha made an attack on the pāṇḍavas. At once the devas made him blind and thus helped the pāṇḍavas. That place later became famous as Lohaṇapura. (skanda purāṇa 1, 2, 65)

लोह

LOHA . II An ancient place of india. arjuna conquered this place during his victory march. (Śloka 25, Chapter 27, Sabhā Parva).

लोहमेखला

LOHAMEKHALĀ . A follower of subrahmaṇya. (Chapter 46, Śloka 18, śalya Parva).

लोहवक्त्र

LOHAVAKTRA . A soldier of subrahmaṇya. (Śloka 75, Chapter 45, śalya Parva).

लोहित १

LOHITA I . (rohita). Son of hariścandra. (For details see under hariścandra).

लोहित २

LOHITA II . A king of ancient india. This king was conquered by arjuna. (Śloka 17, Chapter 27, Vana Parva).

लोहित ३

LOHITA III . A serpent. This serpent is a member of the court of varuṇa. (Śloka 8, Chapter 9, Sabhā Parva).

लोहितगंगा

LOHITAGAṄGĀ . A place of Purāṇic fame. śrī kṛṣṇa killed five notorious demons like pañcaja and virūpākṣa at this place. (Chapter 33, Dākṣiṇātya Pāṭha, Sabhā Parva).

लोहिताक्ष १

LOHITĀKṢA I . One the four Pārṣadas given to subrahmaṇya by brahmā. The other three are nandisena, ghaṇṭākarṇa and kumudamālī. (Śloka 24, Chapter 45, śalya Parva).

लोहिताक्ष २

LOHITĀKṢA II . A sage who was a ṛtvik in the sarpasatra of janamejaya. It was this sage who prophesied through a brahmin that the sarpasatra would never be complete. (āśramavāsika parva, Ch 45. Verse 15; Ch 51. Verse 6; Ch 53. Verse 12).

लोहिताक्षी

LOHITĀKṢĪ . A follower of subrahmaṇya. (Śloka 22, Chapter 46, śalya Parva).

लोहितारणी

LOHITĀRAṆĪ . A river of Purāṇic fame of ancient india (Śloka 18, Chapter 9, bhīṣma parva, M.B.).

लोहिताश्व

LOHITĀŚVA (rohitāśva) . Son of hariścandra. (See under hariścandra).

लोहितायनी

LOHITĀYANĪ . Daughter of Red Sea and one of the foster-mothers of subrahmaṇya. lohitāyanī was a worshipper of the Kadamba tree. (Śloka 40, Chapter 280, Vana Parva).

लोहित्या

LOHITYĀ . A great river. The present name of this river is Brahmaputra. The devī of this river sits in the court of varuṇa and worships him. (Śloka 22, Chapter 9, Sabhā Parva).
